role: Editorial introductions; formal source records remain the governing meanings.

by_term.Actor: An identifiable participant in Lab activity. Concrete participants, such as people, teams or agents, use their own governed records; Actor is the general classification.
by_term.Admission Transaction: Applies an already authorized bundle of record changes together, checks its exact targets and starting state, and records the result. It adds no permission of its own.
by_term.Agent: An operational participant that works through an identified instance and session, with a job, prepared information, tools and stated permissions.
by_term.Agent Action: A saved record of one proposed, attempted, completed, rejected or failed operation, identifying the agent instance and session responsible.
by_term.Agent Assignment: Records the job or responsibility assigned to an agent, including what it concerns, its owner, time limits, expected participation and stopping conditions.
by_term.Agent Capability: Describes a class of attempts an agent can technically make, with input, output, evidence and failure requirements. Ability does not itself grant permission.
by_term.Agent Instance: One concrete operational agent, with its behavior profile, implementation, capabilities and accountability identified. A machine instance belongs to one session and ends with it.
by_term.Agent Profile: Reusable, versioned rules for expected agent behavior, inputs, outputs, tools, evidence, escalation and stopping. The profile is saved project knowledge, not a live agent or permission grant.
by_term.Agent Reflection: A revisable diagnostic interpretation of recorded agent work and evidence. It states an interpretation for review, separately from observations, established findings or decisions.
by_term.Agent Session: One temporary working period that identifies the agent instance, assignment, information views, policies, permissions, resources and termination conditions. It owns that instance’s working memory.
by_term.Append-Only Event Ledger: An ordered event-recording pattern that retains earlier entries and records corrections as new entries. Retrying the same action must not count it twice.
by_term.Artifact: An identifiable, typed and versioned record produced or maintained for a purpose, with its owner, origins, lifecycle and ways to validate it stated.
by_term.Artifact Lifetime: Distinguishes temporary work products from standing references maintained over time. Temporary work may preserve competing interpretations; standing references must not retain live simultaneous contradictions. Recorded supersession is permitted.
by_term.Artifact Surface Classification: Requires every governed file to have exactly one declared role, including the package manifest itself. A folder location cannot silently determine that role.
by_term.Artifact Type: The contract for records of a particular kind: their meaning bindings, designated machine format, human views and checks. Accepting the type does not accept every record using it.
by_term.Artifact Type Registry: The catalog identifying record-type contracts, exact source locations and whether particular versions have been accepted. It supports explicit type selection.
by_term.Artifact Type Request: A request explaining a gap when no available type contract fits. The request starts review; it does not itself supply the missing accepted type.
by_term.Artifact Type Resolution: Identifies a particular accepted record-type contract using an exact reference or declared identifying field. It reports unresolved or ambiguous results rather than guessing from filenames.
by_term.Authority: The scoped right or responsibility to decide what a term, rule, record, relationship, result or change may count as for a stated purpose.
by_term.Authority Boundary: Records the exact limits of an owner’s decision rights. It determines what may be authorized, separately from where a workflow asks the owner.
by_term.Authority Claim: A statement of a particular right or responsibility within a stated scope, with the basis needed to assess it. Stating a claim does not validate it.
by_term.Authority Model: Describes which kinds of records and decisions can govern a purpose, who owns them and the limits separating their authority.
by_term.Authority Promotion: A staged route from source evidence and a proposal to owner-reviewed authority. Generalizing domain work requires additional exercise, challenge and review; later adoption has its own scope.
by_term.Authority Surface: An identified project document or record permitted to govern meaning, structural rules, acceptance decisions or contracts within a specified scope.
by_term.Axiom: A foundational proposition about the world or domain that the model takes as given and builds around. It is not a requirement on the system’s behavior; revising it requires reviewing what depends on it.
by_term.Bounded Context: A named area of a domain model in which terms and rules have a deliberately consistent meaning. Separate Context Maps record relationships to other areas.
by_term.Bounded Self-Application Invariant: A governed process may be applied to its own outputs only when every recursive step identifies its scope, owner, review gate, carried state or residue, how results will be recombined, and a stopping condition.
by_term.Canonical Package Home: The designated package containing material that changes together. Distinct capabilities, contexts, products and runtime records remain separately identified within it; other catalogs point to it rather than keeping competing master copies.
by_term.Canonical Package Manifest: Declares the package’s identity, what changes together, each file’s role and any nested lifecycle boundaries. Folder layout does not substitute for those declarations.
by_term.Canonical Representation Invariant: Requires one designated machine representation for each artifact and an owner-approved process-origin declaration for its kind. Generated human views do not gain independent authority, and origin assurance does not establish truth.
by_term.Capability Instance: A locally owned realization of a reusable capability, explicitly linked to its parent while retaining a separate identity and authority.
by_term.Capability Realization Binding: Links a particular product-capability version to implementation versions and their roles, compatibility, adoption and supporting evidence. The link alone does not prove adoption, deployment or value.
by_term.Challenge Contract: States who may contest which revisions, acceptable reasons and evidence, response ownership, timing and resolution rules. Filing a challenge does not automatically suspend a record.
by_term.Challenge Event: Records that an eligible challenger contested a particular revision under a particular Challenge Contract. It is not the resolution or an automatic change of status.
by_term.Claim-Support Compatibility Invariant: A claim’s strength, status or authority effect must stay within the proof, evidence, owner decision or accepted premise offered to support it. Partial or missing support must remain explicit.
by_term.Classification: Assigns a particular thing and version to declared categories and values. Categorizing it does not change its identity or establish cause, success or authority.
by_term.Classification Assignment: Records a particular classification value for a particular subject version under an identified scheme and axis, with its basis. Correction creates a successor assignment.
by_term.Classification Axis: One declared question used to classify something, such as its kind or lifecycle state. Its answers have a distinct decision or checking purpose.
by_term.Classification Orthogonality Invariant: Requires classification questions to remain distinct, with dependencies stated explicitly. A convenient duplicate label must not become a second source of truth.
by_term.Classification Scheme: Defines the classification questions, allowed values, applicability and assignment rules. A revised scheme does not silently reinterpret older assignments.
by_term.Classification Value: One allowed answer within a particular classification question and scheme version. A similar label elsewhere does not make it the same value.
by_term.Closed Authority-Kind Invariant: Requires authority-bearing kinds to belong to an explicitly closed allowed set, with an owner and declared lifecycle. A new kind is blocked pending an owner decision; the source distinguishes this rule from still-pending deterministic enforcement.
by_term.Communication Preference: Records a preference about presentation, language, detail or interaction under stated conditions, including expiry and overrides. It does not grant authority or become a policy by being saved.
by_term.Conformance: An evidence-supported statement that a particular thing meets a particular contract within stated conditions. Passing some checks does not establish broader compliance.
by_term.Constitution: A versioned, owner-scoped rulebook for selected kinds of subject. Its requirements apply only after the exact version and scope are adopted and the subject matches its selectors; loading it into context does not adopt it.
by_term.Constraint-Cycle Safety Invariant: Forbids a connection from both constraining another subject’s values and participating in a cycle without an explicit acyclicity constraint. Proposals needing both properties must stop for schema governance and contextuality-obstruction review before influencing work.
by_term.Contestability Policy: Declares how a governed object’s meaning, state or claims may be challenged and who handles the response.
by_term.Context: A stable frame of relevance and interpretation for one purpose, anchored to exactly one product and, when applicable, one project and one goal, with explicit consumers and source rules.
by_term.Context Lineage Record: Records how an earlier context identity relates to its successors and which meanings were preserved or changed.
by_term.Context Map: Owns the declared directional relationship between particular Bounded Context versions. Those contexts do not maintain rival copies of that relationship’s membership.
by_term.Context Migration Manifest: A reviewable plan identifying context material to move, destinations, changes, stopping conditions and how to reverse the move.
by_term.Context Profile: Reusable rules for constructing and resolving contexts, including allowed anchors, sources, freshness and succession. It is not a particular product- or project-bound context or a resolved view.
by_term.Context Request: States what an identified task or consumer needs from a context, including selection and freshness conditions, without changing that context’s identity.
by_term.Context View: The fixed information selection produced for one request at identified source versions, with exclusions and conditions for use and refresh.
by_term.Contract: A versioned statement of requirements, permissions, prohibitions, interfaces, evidence and breach handling for identified parties or things. The statement is separate from its implementation or proof of compliance.
by_term.Coordination Context: A saved frame for work: exactly one product, optional project and goal references, a stable purpose, intended users and source rules. It can refer to independently owned domain models without merging them.
by_term.Craft Method: A governed way of building systems through smaller construction steps whose results can be recombined, while preserving purpose, choices, evidence and unresolved work.
by_term.CyberAlchemy Construction Method: The governed construction path from a product intent to an implementation that can be reviewed, assessed, operated and changed.
by_term.CyberAlchemy Repository Identity: Identifies the earlier CyberAlchemy v2 repository candidate and its purpose of consolidating dispersed work into a reviewable base. The definition is not evidence of a completed stable release.
by_term.Decision: A recorded authority act selecting an outcome or permitted effect for specified things within stated limits. The choice and evidence that its effect occurred are separate facts.
by_term.Decision Bundle: Presents several specific decisions in one review while retaining each decision’s owner, targets and consequences. Shared presentation does not expand authority.
by_term.Decision Checkpoint: A position in a workflow where required decisions or requests can be presented together. It determines where the question appears, not what the reviewer may authorize.
by_term.Decision Request Set: Groups specific questions for one interaction while preserving each request’s owner, scope, target and intended effect.
by_term.Decision Scope: The specified subjects, actions, effects, time limits and exclusions covered by one decision. Similar names or shared ownership do not broaden it.
by_term.Definition: An owner-controlled record stating exactly what a term means, where that meaning applies and how drift can be challenged. Acceptance is separate from draft checks or explanatory wording.
by_term.Delegation: An explicit permission from an authorized owner or principal for an agent to perform named actions within stated scope and time limits. The delegator must possess the permission being delegated.
by_term.Derived Refresh: Regenerates and validates a view from unchanged designated machine input under an exact generator binding. It creates no meaning revision, representation revision, decision or authority effect; generator changes are governed separately.
by_term.Discipline: A recurring practice across capabilities with evidence, a steward and a hardening route. Recurrence supports review but does not itself promote the practice to authority.
by_term.Drift Assessment: Compares declared and observed versions, meanings, connections, behavior or freshness at a specified time. Finding a mismatch does not establish its cause or permission to fix it.
by_term.Effect: A stated change to state, rights, obligations, external conditions or interpretation. Intending, authorizing, attempting and observing that change are separate facts.
by_term.Evaluation: Executes stated checks against identified inputs and records each result, including checks that could not be evaluated.
by_term.Evidence: Inspectable material bearing on a particular claim within stated conditions. Support or opposition must be assessed; the material does not decide acceptance by itself.
by_term.Evidence Set: Organizes evidence for a stated question, including material against the conclusion and gaps in support.
by_term.Exact Publication Authorization Invarian: For private material, each source owner must authorize an exact candidate slice and its permitted use. After private generation and validation, the publishing principal separately approves the exact finished bytes, audience, channel and claim limits.
by_term.Experience Evidence Formation Method: A route for turning interface observations and lessons into proposed reusable rules through evidence, later use, challenge and owner review.
by_term.Experiment Design: The plan specifying conditions, variables, measurements, comparisons and stopping rules before an experiment is claimed to have run.
by_term.Experiment Run: A record of one execution of an experiment design, including conditions, deviations and observations.
by_term.Failure: An evidence-supported inability of a particular thing and version to meet a specified requirement under stated conditions. It does not alone establish cause, blame or permission to change the system.
by_term.Failure Assessment: Examines a particular failure or group of failures, keeping occurrence, pattern, cause, impact, containment, recovery and uncertainty distinct. Recovery can coexist with an unresolved cause.
by_term.Failure Control Binding: Associates a particular failure-pattern version with one control and its primary role: prevent, detect, contain, recover or compensate. It records intent, not proof of execution or effectiveness.
by_term.Failure Mode: A reusable description of a distinct possible failure under stated conditions. It may exist before any actual failure is observed.
by_term.Failure Occurrence: Records evidence of one actual or suspected failure episode involving a particular version and requirement. The cause and wider consequences may remain uncertain.
by_term.Feedback Record: A saved response such as a correction, rejection, preference or requirement change, with its source, target, time and context identified. Feedback is not automatically fact or permission.
by_term.Finding: An attributable conclusion stating what the evidence supports and its limits. It is not automatically a decision or policy.
by_term.Four-Facet Artifact Invariant: Requires governed actions to identify classification, schema, a human-continuation view and a machine-checkable view. Missing aspects must be recorded with an owner and whether work may continue, wait or is blocked.
by_term.Gate: An owner-scoped checkpoint deciding or routing whether a candidate may proceed, proceed with named risk, stop or defer. Its criteria, evidence, verdicts and consequences must be explicit.
by_term.Generated Output: A reproducible result from exact inputs and a particular generator version, with origin and consistency checks. An explicit type contract can designate it as a canonical record; generation does not make it a second semantic authority.
by_term.Goal: The future result a project seeks, with the conditions and evidence its owner needs before declaring achievement.
by_term.Govern UX/UI Knowledge: The process for retaining and reviewing interface evidence and lessons without treating appearance, screenshots or passing browser checks as proof of human experience.
by_term.Governance Event History: A history retaining complete governance observations linked to particular semantic events and upstream evidence. It records governance state; it does not create policies or decisions.
by_term.Governance-Axis Independence Invariant: Requires kind, status, evidence confidence, commitment confidence, provenance and owner to remain distinct when they matter to a decision. One dimension cannot silently answer another: acceptance does not establish strong evidence.
by_term.Governed Model: A versioned model of concepts, rules, structures or behavior with scope, owner, sources, assumptions, checks, lifecycle and challenge handling. It is not automatically an ontology, implementation or accepted truth.
by_term.Hypothesis: A proposition framed so evidence can test it. It remains distinct from an assumption already chosen as a premise.
by_term.Identity Carrier: The designated record identifying one particular thing. Folder names, ownership and connections cannot silently change that identity.
by_term.Identity Claim: States that a reference belongs to a person and the basis for believing it. Establishing identity does not grant a role or permission.
by_term.Identity Lineage: Records continuity and change across a rename or successor, with explicit ownership. Similar names or contents are insufficient to establish the same identity.
by_term.Identity Relation: An explicit relationship between separately identified things. Linking them does not make them identical or transfer authority.
by_term.Implementation: A versioned technical realization with sources, owner, interfaces, build or deployment information and evidence. Its existence does not prove live operation, compliance or value.
by_term.Improvement Signal: An identifiable indication of a possible weakness or opportunity that can be grouped, assessed and routed. It does not yet establish recurrence, cause, benefit or permission.
by_term.Improvement Target: An owner-reviewed, deduplicated statement of a recurring weakness or opportunity routed into research, experiments or technical changes. It does not authorize automatic self-modification.
by_term.Incident: Coordinates response and accountability for related failures or uncertain impacts, with ownership, timeline, decisions and closure. Closing it retains evidence and unresolved obligations.
by_term.Intent: The desired outcome and constraints before a particular solution is selected.
by_term.Intent Resolution: An owner’s choice of how to address one intent and how satisfaction will be assessed. Selection does not prove delivery or authorize unrelated work.
by_term.Interface Claim-Support Compatibility In: Browser evidence can support claims about what occurred on a page. Claims about human understanding, trust or preference need suitable human evidence.
by_term.Invariant: A condition the system must preserve. It constrains system behavior, separately from an axiom about the world and the rules used to enforce it.
by_term.Ledger: An ordered collection of identifiable entries with declared entry, integrity, correction, reconciliation and retention rules. It is not inherently append-only, true or authoritative.
by_term.Lesson Application: Records use or deliberate non-use of one lesson version in later work. Showing, selecting, using and benefiting from the lesson are separate facts.
by_term.Lesson Outcome Assessment: Compares a lesson’s predicted benefit and contradicting conditions with evidence from a particular application. Task completion or self-report alone does not establish benefit.
by_term.Measurement Method: A reproducible procedure for measuring a property under stated conditions, with units, tools, calibration, computation and uncertainty handling identified.
by_term.Measurement Result: The saved values and evidence from one execution of a particular measurement method against a particular subject version. It is separate from the method and later interpretation.
by_term.Method: A repeatable, governed transformation with inputs, actions and checkable results that preserves unresolved work.
by_term.Model Instance Binding: Records how one local model instance relates to a particular shared parent model, including inherited requirements, permitted extensions and adoption. Their identities, owners and authority remain separate.
by_term.Observation: Records what was seen or measured during a Research or Experiment Run, with conditions and uncertainty, before interpreting its meaning.
by_term.Ontology: A governed structured model of concepts, things and relationships, with rules for representation, evidence, lifecycle and use.
by_term.Ontology Cut: A rebuilt, fixed and consistent recorded ontology state at particular positions in its semantic and governance histories. It does not replace those histories as reconstruction sources.
by_term.Ontology Edge: An independently identified graph connection representing a particular global Typed Relation or a separately declared ontology-local relationship. A local edge does not become a global connection.
by_term.Ontology Manifest: The designated identity and configuration record for an ontology, identifying its model, owners, policies, connection registry and runtime choices. It is not a snapshot of all represented objects.
by_term.Ontology Node: A separately identified representation of one particular thing and version inside an ontology, with sources and governance details. It does not replace the represented thing or prove its claims.
by_term.Ontology View: A fixed selection from one consistent recorded ontology state for an identified purpose and consumer, with source positions, exclusions and use and expiry conditions.
by_term.Operational Learning Cycle: Turns identifiable agent work into reviewed interpretations, proposed advice, later applications and outcome assessments. Improvements require their own owner-routed changes.
by_term.Operational Lesson: Versioned advice for future project work with evidence, applicability, exclusions, predicted benefit and a result that would contradict it. Saving advice does not turn it into a policy or permission.
by_term.Operational Observation: A record of information observed during ordinary project work outside research or experiment-specific observations. It does not alone establish cause or the required response.
by_term.Parent-Instance Authority Separation Inv: Keeps the owner and authority of a shared parent model separate from those of a local instance. An explicit binding records their relationship without letting either silently rewrite the other.
by_term.Person: A human being, separately identified from accounts, roles and records describing them.
by_term.Person Reference: The minimum record needed to identify a person for a stated purpose, without duplicating their full identity record.
by_term.Policy: A versioned rule set issued within a particular authority scope, specifying required or prohibited actions and handling. It does not execute itself or grant authority beyond its issuer.
by_term.Preference Application Assessment: Checks whether a particular communication preference applies to one output, conflicts, is overridden or cannot be followed. It does not prove satisfaction or rewrite the preference.
by_term.Premise: An explicit assumption selected for the present work. It remains identified so conclusions can be revisited if it changes.
by_term.Principal: An identity recognized within a particular authentication, authorization, ownership or accountability boundary. Recognition at one boundary does not grant rights at others.
by_term.Principal Reference: A minimal reference allowing a record to resolve the relevant principal identity and integrity information without copying the full identity record.
by_term.Product: The continuing offering that promises value to participants. Particular projects and implementations serve it while retaining their own identities.
by_term.Product Capability: An outcome the product should enable for identified consumers, separate from the technology selected to provide it.
by_term.Product Thesis: States who the product serves, the expected value, important constraints and evidence that could change those propositions.
by_term.Project: A continuing coordination identity for a particular effort, keeping its goals, decisions, evidence and work together across changes to plans or files.
by_term.Project Governance Event History: Retains why particular Project State changes were accepted, linking authorization and evidence to exact change events. It does not alter the resulting state or originate authority.
by_term.Project Semantic Event History: Retains complete resulting Project State changes and their predecessors in order so state can be reconstructed. It records what changed, not whether the change was authorized.
by_term.Project State: The project’s saved records, definitions, decisions, evidence, histories and connections. It belongs to the project and its record owners, not private agent memory. Included records retain their own standing; accepting the state does not automatically promote its sources.
by_term.Projection Specification: Identifies when a concept needs a governed view to preserve its evidence, relationships, lifecycle, ownership and challenge behavior. That view does not itself decide authority.
by_term.Prototype-First DomainSpec Construction: Learn with explicit prototypes, then freeze and assess a particular product only when its model is coherent. Product approval and real-world authority decisions remain separate.
by_term.Provenance: A traceable account of where information came from, who or what produced it and the transformations and versions involved.
by_term.Relation Kind: A versioned rule for one directional connection meaning, a finite set of allowed source–target kind pairs and required additional details. Separate lists do not permit every combination.
by_term.Repository Migration Manifest: An exact moving plan identifying source items, destinations, content fingerprints, collision handling and rollback scope. It neither performs nor authorizes the move.
by_term.Representation Revision: A new designated machine encoding or representation contract that preserves the artifact’s accepted meaning. Earlier contents remain recorded rather than being silently overwritten.
by_term.Research Inquiry: Defines a research question, scope, source rules, method and stopping conditions before the investigation runs.
by_term.Research Run: Records what a particular research attempt actually did, with its selected inputs, method and results.
by_term.Residue: Meaningful information, distinctions or obligations that remain unresolved or were not preserved by the current representation or work.
by_term.Residue Escalation Method: Records an unresolved gap, its evidence and owner route, then refers it to a participant able to decide or repair it.
by_term.Residue Measurement: Measures distinctions, uncertainty or information loss exposed by a declared operation. The mathematical interpretation, measure, scope and status must be stated before it influences governance.
by_term.Responsibility: What a participant must answer for. Responsibility is distinct from permission to authorize particular actions.
by_term.Review: An identifiable assessment of particular versions against stated questions, criteria and evidence. Review is separate from acceptance, execution or permission to apply changes.
by_term.Role: A named position and its responsibilities, separately from the person or team occupying it.
by_term.Role Assignment: Records who holds a role, within which scope and time interval. It does not silently add team membership or authority.
by_term.Root-Axis Independence Invariant: Keeps separately governed dimensions—such as status, owner, representation and validation—independently variable unless an explicit rule relates them. Advancing one must not silently advance or authorize another.
by_term.Schema: Specifies permitted structure, fields, constraints and connections. Structural validity does not establish truth, ownership, permission or acceptance.
by_term.Schema Evolution Invariant: Requires schema changes to retain provenance and declare how mistakes will be detected, or record the unresolved validation gap and its owner.
by_term.Semantic Epoch: An owner-selected version of an artifact’s governing meaning. A material meaning change requires a successor; changed encoding alone does not.
by_term.Semantic Event History: Retains complete resulting meaning-bearing states for an ontology subject in order for reconstruction. Its generated snapshots do not become competing history sources.
by_term.Semantic Primitive: A base semantic kind available for building more specialized kinds under the declared model.
by_term.Session Memory: Temporary working information owned by exactly one agent session. It ends with that session and cannot be shared as hidden private memory with another.
by_term.Source: An identifiable origin from which information or a claim was obtained, with a resolvable reference and integrity boundary. Origin alone does not establish truth, freshness or authority.
by_term.Source-Ledgered Consolidation: Combines dispersed work while recording each source group, its authority status and its review route. Synthesis and copying do not themselves grant authority.
by_term.Stable Repository: A repository meeting declared criteria for a trustworthy, understandable and usable base. A release still needs evidence and the appropriate owner decision.
by_term.Stable Repository Stewardship: The ongoing maintenance that preserves repository clarity, trustworthy source selection and readiness after initial construction.
by_term.Team: A continuing group identity that remains distinct from its changing membership.
by_term.Team Membership: Records a person’s belonging to a team for a period, separately from their role, responsibilities or authority.
by_term.Tool: An invocable resource with a versioned interface, input and output requirements, failure limits and evidence route. Availability does not grant permission or prove successful use.
by_term.Traceability: The ability to follow explicit links between purpose, sources, decisions, changes, results and subsequent work.
by_term.Typed Connection Extension Rule: Specifies how new global connection kinds or permitted pairs are declared, reviewed and admitted with endpoint contracts, ownership and challenge rules. Local graph edges and endpoint registration do not create global permission.
by_term.Typed Coupling Invariant: Requires a dependency, influence, constraint or co-change between separately governed subjects to be an explicit typed relation with named endpoints, direction, meaning, owner, evidence and validation or promotion effect.
by_term.Typed Relation: One identified global connection between specific source and target versions under an accepted Relation Kind and allowed pair, with required details and governance. A graph projection does not create or validate it.
by_term.Ubiquitous Language: The shared vocabulary used to discuss and build within one Bounded Context, where its meanings are deliberately consistent.
by_term.User Decision Preference: A user’s preferred review position for a particular workflow, limited to the positions that workflow permits. An invalid explicit preference blocks resolution rather than silently falling back.
by_term.Validation: Executes specified checks on specified inputs. Passing reports those checks, not every possible requirement or owner acceptance.
by_term.Validation Receipt: Records what was checked, against which requirements, with which tool and results. It is evidence of validation, not an approval stamp.
by_term.Withdrawal Record: Permanently records withdrawal or retirement of an identifier, its reason, owner decision, history and any declared successor. It does not erase history, reuse the identity or automatically replace another record.
by_term.Work: An identified activity with purpose, owner, inputs, participants, expected result, constraints and outcome trace. It does not itself establish permission, completion or benefit.
by_term.Work Outcome Assessment: Compares the stated expected result of a work item or action with evidence of the observed result. It does not by itself establish lesson value or broader product benefit.
by_term.Work-State Continuity Capability: Supports resuming work from saved state and records instead of relying on a participant’s recollection of the conversation.
by_term.Workflow: Coordinates ordered operations within or across product-feature boundaries. Its evaluation can propose recovery; a separate executor invokes the specified operation bindings.
by_term.Workflow Decision Profile: Defines whether a workflow requires a person’s decision, the allowed review positions and conditions for continuation. Configuring it does not perform a decision or grant authority.

literature_notes_by_title.W3C PROV-DM: A provenance model records entities, activities and participants: what existed, what was done and who was involved. It helps explain tracing a Lab record to its origins; the comparison grants no Lab authority.
literature_notes_by_title.NIST SP 800-162, ABAC: Attribute-based access control evaluates a requesting participant, the target, the requested operation and relevant conditions. It helps explain actor permissions, one part of the Lab’s broader authority model.
literature_notes_by_title.Saltzer and Schroeder, Basic Principles: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed for the task. Checking access at each use helps explain why delegation has limits and why previous permission does not settle every later action.
literature_notes_by_title.W3C SHACL: SHACL describes constraints on graph data, such as which fields and connections a node may have. It provides a comparison for structural validation; these essays do not establish that the Lab implements SHACL.
literature_notes_by_title.Martin Fowler, Event Sourcing: Event sourcing preserves changes as events and reconstructs state from their history. This helps explain replay and derived state. The Lab also records the authority for governed changes.
literature_notes_by_title.Martin Fowler, Bounded Context: A bounded context defines where a particular model and vocabulary apply. It helps explain how the same word can have different scoped meanings and why connections between contexts need explicit rules.
literature_notes_by_title.Park et al., Generative Agents: This simulation studies agents using observations, retrieved memories, reflections and plans. It provides an example of external memory architecture; its results do not establish business reliability or Lab conformance.
literature_notes_by_title.Lean reference, Validating a Lean Proof: A proof checker can establish a formal result about a stated theorem. Whether that theorem captures the intended real-world meaning is a separate question. The essays preserve this distinction when discussing formal assurance.
literature_notes_by_title.Mensh and Kording, Ten simple rules for: The editorial method emphasizes a central contribution, the reader’s existing knowledge and a logical progression. Those ideas inform the structure of each essay.
